business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (PRC) - Taiwan-invested Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise formation jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (PRC socialist legal system with strong regulatory overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Bilateral Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (2012)
Agreement between the Straits Exchange Foundation and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits on Verification of Notarized Documents (1993)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2019 amendment); Administrative Measures on Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Material and Transaction Records Preservation (PBOC Order [2022] No. 1); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information Registration and Management (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (SAMR Order No. 10, adopted 2021); Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020); Company Law of the PRC (2023 revision).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Legal Person Business License
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For domestic filing in PRC: original plus notarised copy accepted. For use abroad in a Hague Apostille Convention state: notarisation by a PRC notary office followed solely by apostille from the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorised provincial foreign affairs office. For use abroad in a non-Hague state: notarisation by a PRC notary office followed solely by consular legalisation through the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the destination state embassy/consulate. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / No-Record of Administrative Penalty
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For domestic use: official printed copy with QR code. For foreign use in a Hague state: PRC notarisation + PRC apostille only. For foreign use in a non-Hague state: PRC notarisation + consular legalisation only. Apostille and consular legalisation are parallel alternatives and must not be combined on one document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders' meeting of the WFOE and PRC notary office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For domestic filing: notarised Chinese charter. For international use: notarised charter plus apostille only for Hague-state recipients; notarised charter plus consular legalisation only for non-Hague recipients. Do not chain apostille with consular legalisation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Formation and Bank Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan parent company's board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For PRC filing: Taiwan notarisation followed by verification through the Straits Exchange Foundation and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits; no apostille or consular legalisation is required under the cross-strait instrument-verification arrangement. For use in a non-Hague destination outside mainland China: Taiwan notarisation followed solely by consular legalisation at the destination state's consular/embassy post. Apostille is not permissible because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention contracting party.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A Taiwanese commercial bank maintaining the parent company's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For PRC corporate-bank account opening: Taiwan notarisation and cross-strait SEF/ARATS verification are the normal path. For any use outside mainland China in a non-Hague state: Taiwan notarisation plus consular legalisation only. For use in a Hague state where the issuing bank is in a member country, apostille by the member country's competent authority may be used, but never in conjunction with consular legalisation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Information Registration Form and Supporting Identification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PBOC/SAMR Beneficial Owner Information Registration System, supported by notarised identity documents of all UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic PRC filing requires no apostille/consular process. If UBO records must be furnished to a foreign regulator or bank in a Hague state: notarised UBO pack plus apostille only. If the foreign regulator/bank is in a non-Hague state: notarised UBO pack plus consular legalisation only. Never apply both authentication modes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every shareholder, UBO, director, legal representative, authorised signatory and major counterparty must be screened before onboarding and continuously against the UN Security Council consolidated terrorist and sanctions lists; OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists; PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Commerce, and PBOC restrictive lists; the CFMS high-risk watchlist; and all applicable local regulatory blacklists. PEPs, including family members and close associates, require senior-management approval, documented source of wealth and source of funds, enhanced due diligence and transaction monitoring. Any reasonable suspicion must be filed as a Suspicious Transaction Report to the CFMS without tipping off. All screening events and results must be preserved in an auditable log.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) - SAMR Enterprise Name Online Self-Service Declaration Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE must have a statutory Chinese-language name; the English name is ancillary. The Chinese name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division plus distinctive name plus industry or business characteristics plus organisational form. Pinyin romanisation is permitted only for the ancillary English name and must not alter the meaning of the registered Chinese characters. Any transliteration that implies state affiliation, false geographical origin or a regulated financial business is prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days after receiving a formal rejection, the applicant may submit a revised name declaration through the same SAMR platform or apply for administrative reconsideration before the issuing market-regulation authority. The appeal must specify the proposed Chinese name, its four-tier components, the business scope and the registrability basis under the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration. If the authority affirms the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. All submission numbers, rejection notices and screen captures should be preserved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: SAMR and the tax authorities generally reject a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox for a payroll SaaS WFOE. The registered address must be a fixed, physical premises where statutory books, payroll client files, employment records, financial accounts and data-processing equipment are kept. Some free-trade zones permit short-term address registration through an approved address service for three to six months, but tax registration, VAT invoice issuance and bank payroll debit-authorization reviews will require an actual lease, office signage, local staff and on-site server or cloud-account management controls. A commercial address with no physical staff occupation will be treated as a high-risk indicator.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) lease or ownership certificate matching the registered address; (2) office spaces, desks, IT equipment, filing cabinets and company sign; (3) employees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.), Articles 2, 99, 128, 156, 161, 171, 172, 192, 203, 216, 278; Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, Article 73; Regulations on the Permission of Investment in Taiwan from the Mainland Area, Articles 4, 6 and 8; Company Registration and Administration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (mainland investment permission) and Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, R.O.C. (Taiwan).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form together with Articles of Incorporation, director and supervisor consent forms, and CPA capital verification report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for ISIC 6201. Taiwan law imposes no minimum paid-in capital for a mainland-invested company limited by shares. The full subscribed capital must be paid in before registration; where paid-in capital exceeds NT$1,000,000, a certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report. No blocked escrow account is required for this software-only business; funds must be deposited into a temporary capital account opened in the Company's name and remain there until the CPA verification is issued.

RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation of the Company, as submitted to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, are adopted and ratified in their entirety; the authorized share capital of the Company is fixed at NT$[●], divided into [●] shares with a par value of NT$[●] each, and the initial paid-in capital is NT$[●], fully subscribed and paid in by the sole shareholder as of the date hereof. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name A], [Name B] and [Name C] are appointed as the first directors of the Company, and [Name D] is appointed as the first supervisor, each to hold office until the earlier of resignation, removal, death, or the third annual general meeting following this resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name A] is appointed Chairman, [Name B] is appointed President and General Manager, and [Name C] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, with authority, acting jointly or severally as specified in the board authorization matrix, to execute banking documents, commercial contracts, and regulatory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [●], [District], Taipei City, Taiwan, R.O.C., as the principal place of business and address for service of legal process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairman, President, and Chief Financial Officer, each acting singly for ordinary administration and jointly for transactions exceeding NT$[●], are authorized to open and maintain bank accounts with [●] Bank, to sign account opening forms and signatory mandates, to designate authorized signatories, and to operate the Company accounts including wire transfers and direct debit arrangements in connection with the payroll automation software business. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Mainland Area Investment Permission and investor pre-qualification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, R.O.C. (Taiwan), via the Invest in Taiwan online portal; mainland China documents must be notarized and verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the Mainland Investment Application through the Investment Commission online portal, naming the mainland China investing entity, proposing a Taiwan company limited by shares, specifying the ISIC 6201 business purpose limited to payroll and staff compliance software, and stating the total paid-in capital. Attach the mainland investor's business registration certificate, audited financial statements for the last fiscal year, bank proof of source of funds, a notarized power of attorney in favor of the Taiwan resident filing agent, and a corporate resolution authorizing the Taiwan investment. The Commission will screen the proposed investment against negative-list restrictions, public interest considerations, capital adequacy, and beneficial ownership. Documents issued in mainland China must be notarized and then verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation before submission. Upon approval, obtain the Mainland Investment Permission Letter, which must be cited in all subsequent company registration filings. If the Commission asks for a supplementary explanation, respond within the prescribed period with a revised investment plan and corrected documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of the mainland Chinese investor
Audited financial statements of the investor for the last fiscal year
Bank certificate confirming source and availability of funds
Notarized power of attorney or board resolution of investor appointing local agent
Passport copies of proposed Taiwan directors
Proposed capital amount and business plan narrative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, suspended, or rejected, the applicant may submit supplementary evidence and an updated investment explanation through the online portal within 14 days. A formal administrative appeal may be filed with the Executive Yuan within 30 days of an adverse decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and execute notarized articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration and Administration Online Application System, Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs; Taiwan notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application proposing at least two English names and one Chinese name for the Taiwan company limited by shares. Ensure the proposed name does not conflict with existing registered companies and does not include prohibited terms. After name approval and issuance of the Mainland Investment Permission Letter, execute the Articles of Incorporation before a Taiwan notary, with the Chinese text controlling. If the investor supplies an English version, the notary may notarize the signatures and the Chinese translation must be certified. The Articles must state the corporate name, business purpose limited to payroll and workforce compliance software, registered office address, authorized and paid-in capital, names of directors and supervisor, and provisions for board meetings and share transfer restrictions. The notarized Articles will be used in the formal registration submission.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application and fee receipt
Draft articles of incorporation in Chinese and English
Proof of registered office address or lease letter of intent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected for similarity, the applicant may amend the proposed name and file a new reservation. If the notarization is queried, correct the legal translation and re-submit the document package to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open temporary capital account, pay-in share capital, and obtain CPA capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank in Taipei; certified public accountant registered with the National Federation of Certified Public Accountants of Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, open a temporary capital account in the Company's name at a licensed bank in Taiwan. Transfer the promised paid-in capital from the mainland Chinese investor to the temporary account using the remittance code and routing instructions provided by the Mainland Investment Permission Letter. The funds must remain in the account until verification. Retain the bank deposit certificate and inward remittance receipt. Instruct a certified public accountant to review the bank confirmation, the Articles of Incorporation, the Mainland Investment Permission Letter, and the share subscription lists, and to issue a Capital Verification Report stating the paid-in capital amount, the share issuance, and that all funds were received and are not from restricted sources. The CPA report is a mandatory filing attachment and must be dated no more than seven days before the company registration application.
required_dossiers: Inward remittance advice or bank receipt showing capital deposit
Capital verification report issued by certified public accountant
List of subscribers and share allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank asks for further explanation of an inward remittance, submit the Mainland Investment Permission Letter and a board resolution to the bank to obtain a revised receipt. If the CPA report cannot be issued because the funds are incomplete, make a supplemental remittance and request a revised verification date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and obtain unified business number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, R.O.C., online company registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal Company Registration Application through the online portal, attaching the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the CPA capital verification report, the Mainland Investment Permission Letter, the board resolution appointing directors and the supervisor, consent forms signed by each director and supervisor, the registered office lease or ownership certificate, and the company name reservation certificate. The application must be completed in Chinese; the English translation may be attached as a supplementary schedule. Pay the registration fee online. The authority will review the filing for statutory consistency and issue the Company Registration Certificate and a Unified Business Number. Thereafter, the company exists as a separate legal entity and may open operating bank accounts and execute contracts.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease agreement or title deed evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a correction notice or rejects the filing due to incomplete attachments, the applicant may amend and resubmit the dossier within the prescribed correction period. A formal appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs or administrative litigation before the Taipei High Administrative Court may be pursued if the rejection is final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, labor insurance, health insurance, and pension program
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor; National Health Insurance Administration, Ministry of Health and Welfare
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Unified Business Number, file the tax registration form to obtain the Business Tax Registration Certificate and VAT identification number. Register as a withholding agent for employee income tax, and register the company as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance for labor insurance and labor pension. Separately register with the National Health Insurance Administration for employees' health insurance. Submit the employment establishment report listing the planned payroll headcount and workplace address, consistent with the payroll automation service scope. For direct debit and wire payment rails, obtain the employer identification certificate and bank account confirmation from the operating bank, and register the payment rails after bank signatory cards are executed.
required_dossiers: First board resolution on banking signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau requests additional evidence of business premises, submit the company registration certificate, registered lease, and operation instructions. For labor insurance delay, the employer may submit a supplementary registration and pay any retrospective premiums together with a remedy explanation to the Bureau.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish operational bank accounts and execute payment rail signatory mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan; regulatory oversight by the Financial Supervisory Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Company Registration Certificate, Unified Business Number, Articles of Incorporation, and the First Board Resolution to open a current operating account in the Company's name. Provide the bank with the beneficial ownership register, identity documents of all directors, and the authorization matrix specifying who may approve wire transfers and direct debits. Execute the bank's account opening agreement and electronic banking services contract. Once the account is active, request the bank to activate direct debit ACH and SWIFT wire services for the payroll automation platform. The bank may conduct a know-your-customer interview at the registered office and require a site inspection confirming active software development operations. Retain the executed bank mandates for annual audit and tax compliance records.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and unified business number
Articles of incorporation and first board resolution
Passport and ARC copies of directors and signatories
Bank account application form and signatory mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's compliance department requests additional documentation under anti-money-laundering rules, provide an enhanced beneficial ownership certificate, a board resolution confirming the payroll automation business model, and a projected transaction volume report. A second bank may be approached if the first bank imposes disproportionate conditions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure software and digital payroll consultancy under ISIC 6201; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no operating or manufacturing permit required for payroll automation software activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan does not mandate EIA for office-based software development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full EIA report or environmental registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the Company generates no industrial wastewater, VOCs, hazardous waste, or air emissions. Office waste shall be disposed by the building manager in accordance with local municipal waste regulations; any standby generator usage must comply with Taipei City air pollution control standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for Civil Defense fire permit because the activity is office-based software development. However, the employer must obtain a standard fire safety inspection certificate for the registered office under the Taiwan Fire Services Act and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including workplace hazard assessment, emergency exits, fire extinguishers, and daily office safety records. No industrial structural load inspection is required for code-writing and data-processing premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, acting through provincial and municipal competent tax offices; online electronic portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Taxation) hosted on the China Tax Administration Information System (CTAIS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The Taiwan investor incorporates the entity as a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE / limited liability company) with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtains the Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), an 18-character code that serves as the mandatory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for all PRC tax registrations. Step 2: Within 30 days of obtaining the license, the WFOE must complete tax registration and the supplementary taxpayer information filing through the Electronic Tax Bureau; the USCC is used as the TIN and VAT registration number, and no separate VAT certificate is issued. Step 3: If the Taiwan investor is a non-resident enterprise earning PRC-source income without a permanent establishment, the WFOE, as withholding agent, must complete non-resident enterprise withholding registration using the investor's Taiwan tax ID and the WFOE's USCC; if treaty or cross-strait tax-arrangement benefits are sought, the investor must also complete non-resident tax registration in the Electronic Tax Bureau with its certificate of incorporation, home-country tax residence certificate, board resolution, and power of attorney appointing a local representative. Step 4: The WFOE must complete payroll/social insurance registration and, before exporting services, foreign exchange receipt registration with a SAFE-authorized bank to support future export zero-rating.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. PRC enterprise income tax law does not provide a check-the-box election, hybrid entity election, or pass-through classification. The WFOE is mandatorily taxed at entity level on worldwide income, and the Taiwan investor cannot elect transparent treatment for PRC tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no economic turnover threshold for VAT registration; every WFOE must register for VAT upon incorporation. The statutory small-scale taxpayer threshold is RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales; taxpayers above this threshold must be registered as general VAT taxpayers. The payroll SaaS platform service, being an information-technology/modern service, is generally subject to the standard 6% VAT rate before application of the export zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax System Phase IV and the fully digitalized electronic invoice (e-invoice) platform. The WFOE must issue VAT invoices through the STA-authorized Electronic Tax Bureau / e-invoice system, transmitting invoice data to the tax authority in real time. Each e-invoice carries a unique digital verification code and is fiscally validated before issuance; API integration is mandatory for fully digitalized e-invoice pilot taxpayers. The tax control system automatically cross-matches invoices, VAT returns, customs declarations, and bank receipts for anti-fraud enforcement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The PRC WFOE qualifies for VAT zero-rating on exported payroll SaaS services supplied to an overseas customer, including a Taiwan-resident customer, when the recipient is located outside mainland China, the services are wholly consumed outside mainland China, and the services are within the statutory catalogue of cross-border zero-rated or VAT-exempt services under the VAT pilot regulations. The taxpayer must be a general VAT taxpayer, issue an export service invoice, receive the foreign-currency or cross-border RMB proceeds, and maintain contractual, delivery, and consumption evidence proving offshore supply. Physical goods exports qualify for 0% only after a completed customs export declaration showing departure from the PRC customs territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry / Export Goods Declaration Form) issued by the General Administration of Customs of China
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or other international transport document evidencing export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or, for PRC purposes, the SAFE-authorized bank's Foreign Exchange Receipt and Export Proceeds Settlement Certificate evidencing repatriation
Signed cross-border service contract and commercial invoice in foreign currency identifying the overseas recipient and place of consumption
Electronic zero-rating service export filing and supporting documentation submitted through the Electronic Tax Bureau
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA audits export zero-rating through the Golden Tax System Phase IV by cross-matching e-invoice data, customs export declarations, VAT returns, and SAFE foreign-exchange records. If the exporter cannot substantiate physical export, offshore consumption, or receipt/repatriation of

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), also known as the Central Bank of Taiwan, acting with the Financial Supervisory Commission under the Management of Foreign Exchange Act and the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan maintains a managed-floating New Taiwan dollar regime with substantially liberalized current-account convertibility. Current-account transactions, including trade in goods and services, dividends, royalties, and employment remuneration, may be remitted freely after filing an electronic foreign-exchange declaration with an authorized bank; no prior central-bank approval is normally required provided the transaction is genuine and documentary evidence is retained. Capital-account items, including equity investment into Taiwan, intra-company loans, acquisition of real estate, and derivative transactions, require a valid prior approval or filing with the CBC, the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs, or another competent authority. Export proceeds must be repatriated to Taiwan through authorized banks within five working days from collection and reported under the export declaration system; the proceeds may be sold to the bank for TWD or credited to a foreign-currency deposit account. Profit remittance by a foreign-invested enterprise is permitted after audited financial statements and tax clearance are presented, but the distribution must be supported by board minutes, a tax payment certificate, and the original foreign-exchange declaration files. In practice, cross-strait investments and remittances from mainland China are subject to additional MOEA Investment Commission screening under the Act Governing Relations between Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, which can lengthen the compliance timeline and require sealed certificates and corporate authorization chains. Overall, TWD is convertible for legitimate business purposes, but the entity must establish a compliance calendar for prior approvals, declaration filings, and documentary retention to avoid delays and penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Measures Governing the Collection and Payment of Export Proceeds, an exporter must repatriate all export foreign-currency receipts to an authorized bank in Taiwan within five working days after the date of payment or the date of negotiation of the transport document, whichever occurs first. The exporter must present the export declaration form or its electronic equivalent and complete the CBC foreign-exchange classification declaration. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter may elect to convert the proceeds into New Taiwan Dollars or to retain the full amount in a foreign-currency deposit account. For cash payments and settlements involving mainland Chinese parties, the bank may impose enhanced documentation and prior regulatory filing requirements before the proceeds are collected.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational New Taiwan Dollar Account and Foreign Currency Deposit Account; Capital Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and NT Dollar Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms are not a viable primary account solution for a Taiwan-registered foreign-invested entity. Taiwan's Banking Act and the CBC's designated-bank framework require multi-currency corporate settlement accounts to be maintained with a licensed domestic bank or an offshore banking unit of a domestic bank. Foreign EMIs are not supervised by the Financial Supervisory Commission and cannot issue TWD settlement accounts, submit CBC foreign-exchange declarations, or participate in the local ACH and interbank clearing systems needed for payroll automation. An EMI may be used only as an auxiliary collection and payout channel to the extent it acts as a white-label distributor of a duly licensed partner bank, and even then, the underlying settlement, FX declaration, and payroll funding must flow through the Taiwan-licensed institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory directors and the ultimate beneficial owners of the WFOE must, in practice, attend a physical identity verification interview at the managing branch of the chosen Taiwan bank. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for a newly formed foreign-invested company; the bank will require an in-person interview with the authorized signatories at the branch in Taiwan, or, for certain banks, at the overseas branch or correspondent office where the foreign investor maintains a qualifying banking relationship. Where a statutory director cannot travel, the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney executed in front of a notary public in the director's jurisdiction, legalized or apostilled as required, but final confirmation through the bank's overseas correspondent or consular channels is typically still required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex cross-strait ownership structure with a mainland Chinese parent and Taiwanese WFOE subsidiary, raising adverse scrutiny under the Act Governing Relations between Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled board resolution authorizing account opening; full corporate registry excerpt of the mainland parent; shareholding register; the MOEA Investment Commission approval or filing letter; audited financial statements of the parent for the latest two years; organizational chart identifying all natural-person beneficial owners; certified copies of passports and resident certificates for all 25 percent or more owners; sworn source-of-wealth statement; and tax-compliance certificates or equivalent corporate tax filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-risk Payroll-SaaS business model processing payroll on behalf of end clients, which may be interpreted as a third-party payment aggregator or unlicensed money service business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business model description; signed client contracts; payroll service agreements; flow-of-funds diagram demonstrating that the WFOE only handles payroll disbursements on an agency basis and does not hold client funds overnight; professional indemnity insurance if held; a legal opinion from a licensed Taiwan attorney confirming that the service is an exempt software and HR service under Taiwan's business registration scope; and the ISIC and NAICS industry classification certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained incoming capital injection and future dividend or royalty outbound remittances triggering cash-flow pattern inconsistencies with the software payroll industry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury forecast model mapping the timing and purpose of inbound parent loans or equity injections to working capital needs; pro-forma cash flow projections; invoices or purchase orders from payroll clients; payroll data processing agreements; tax invoice registers; accountant's certification on the source of funds; and bank statements of the parent confirming the same funds path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse-media risk arising from the mainland parent's presence in a high-risk sector or state-linked industrial ecosystem.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions and watchlist screening certificates from a reputable commercial data provider; shareholder identity declarations; ultimate-beneficial-owner registry; compliance policies and procedures owned by the group; evidence of no restrictive services to designated persons; and a letter of legal responsibility signed by the parent's board confirming no involvement in sanctioned military, espionage, or trade-restricted activities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Taiwan WFOE must be routed through a licensed domestic bank or the bank's offshore banking unit using a SWIFT MT103 payment from the foreign parent. The remittance must cite the approved investment project number or, for a new foreign-invested company, the preliminary registration number issued by the MOEA Investment Commission. The receiving bank will prepare a foreign-exchange declaration using the capital-account purpose code applicable to foreign investment in Taiwan. The WFOE must present the MOEA approval or filing receipt, the parent's board resolution approving the capital injection, and the shareholder loan agreement if the injection is structured as a shareholder loan. Upon receipt, a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report confirming that the funds were received in TWD or in foreign exchange and credited to the WFOE's account; the bank will then file the inward remittance with the CBC and issue a foreign-exchange receipt certificate, which becomes the documentary basis for registration and future dividend remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payroll disbursements and vendor settlements must be executed on the domestic ACH bulk clearing system for New Taiwan Dollar payroll runs, using the automated bulk round-file submission window of the financial information service; cross-border payroll and vendor payments to overseas beneficiaries should be settled through SWIFT MT103, provided the remittance purpose code and payroll support files are retained. For trade-related disbursements where goods or services are documented, Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections may be used, with presentation documents sent through the collecting bank. All outbound wires must be declared on the bank's foreign-exchange declaration platform, and the underlying payroll tax withholdings and employee identification records must be retained to substantiate the payment purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla outright forward foreign-exchange contracts for TWD/USD, TWD/CNY, and TWD/EUR with a Taiwan-licensed bank, supported by a documented underlying trade or investment exposure
FX swaps between TWD and acceptable convertible currencies for cash-flow management, limited to genuine temporary liquidity needs and not for speculative outright positions

Non-deliverable forwards may be considered only where the counterparty is an offshore branch of a recognized bank and only for non-resident entities; Taiwan-resident entities are generally prohibited from participating in offshore NDF markets unless the CBC grants an explicit exemption

Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term foreign-currency capital injections, subject to underlying debt, capital investment, or dividend-flow exposure and to the bank's derivatives product approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Report (AML/CFT Substantial Beneficiaries Form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Department of Commerce, Taiwan (online Company Beneficial Ownership Reporting System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for the preceding calendar year; initial filing due within 30 days of company formation or any subsequent UBO-change event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 50,000 - 500,000 per violation for failure to file or false filing; repeated non-compliance, after notice and grace period, may result in administrative deregistration and strike-off of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (corporate income tax return with audited/supporting financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local district tax authority of Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 May to 31 May for the prior taxable year; CPA-certified filing window is extended to 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of up to 3% per month on underpaid tax (capped at 9%); default interest on arrears; estimated assessment on non-filing; enforced collection; prolonged delinquency can result in administrative dissolution by the tax authority after an outstanding-judgment process

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Salary Withholding Tax Statements (salary withholding remittance declarations and annual withholding certificates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (payroll tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by no later than 31 January for all payroll paid during the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of TWD 750 - 4,500 for each unreported or late-reported withholding certificate; under-withholding gives rise to an additional 15% penalty and recovery of unpaid tax; repeated violations can trigger a payroll audit but do not by themselves lead to corporate strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan's Company Act and Business Entity Accounting Act, a private limited company (WFOE Ltd.) is legally required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor if (i) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 1,000,000); (ii) it qualifies as a public company under the Securities and Exchange Act; (iii) it operates in banking, insurance, securities, financial holding or other regulated sectors irrespective of size; or (iv) the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the national tax authority specifically requires audited financial statements for a particular period. For this non-regulated payroll software SaaS entity, the quantitative balance-sheet trigger is the NT$30M paid-in capital threshold; there are no separate annual turnover or headcount audit triggers under ordinary private-company rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in New Taiwan Dollars under the Taiwan Business Entity Accounting Act, applying Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TW FRS) aligned with IFRS for SMEs/private companies; public issuers apply IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. A private non-listed WFOE may use the SME standard for simplified disclosure where eligible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan AML/CFT regulations require every company (including a WFOE Ltd.) to submit an annual beneficial ownership confirmation by 31 March each calendar year. In addition, any transfer of shareholding or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be reported to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of the triggering event, with a rectified report; the statement must identify the natural-person beneficial owner, nationality, shareholding percentages and control chain. Failure to timely update is subject to the statutory UBO penalty and repeated-filing enforcement.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year (Taipei registered office address and corporate secretarial agent service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 9,000 for a private WFOE with assets at or near the audit threshold; lower if a CPA review instead of full audit is permitted

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (CIT) rate under Article 4 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law, applicable to the resident Chinese WFOE; 15% preferential rate for certified High and New Technology Enterprises and Technology-Advanced Service Enterprises; 20% reduced rate with effective 5%-10% loading for qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprises on taxable income not exceeding RMB 3,000,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying software enterprises (software development and related services, ISIC 6201) enjoy two-year full exemption and three-year 50% reduction (effective 12.5%) from the first profit-making year; R&D expenditure super deduction of 100% under the current policy framework; accelerated depreciation or amortization of software and fixed assets used for R&D; 15% rate for High/New-Technology and Technology-Advanced Service enterprises; interest withholding and dividend relief under the Cross-Strait tax arrangement as applicable to non-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A类) - Main Form A100000 with supporting annex schedules A101010 through A108030, plus the annual Related-Party Transactions Reporting Package (G-series forms); filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax Bureau (企业电子税务局) operating on the Gold Tax Phase IV (金税四期) system, or through certified tax software integrated with e-filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement, one filing per tax year (calendar year for the standard WFOE).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the end of the tax year; for a calendar-year WFOE, no later than 31 May of the following year; quarterly prepayment returns must be filed within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end (15 April, 15 July, 15 October, 15 January).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 1 - 营业收入 Operating Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from payroll SaaS subscriptions, implementation services, maintenance, and payroll automation support, recognized under applicable Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not enter data on the WFOE return; revenue generated from Taiwan parent customers must be fully recognized in the WFOE books and included here; any diversion to offshore accounts is a fatal red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 5 - 管理费用 Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Including payroll costs, social insurance, software amortization, and intra-group service fees paid to the Taiwan parent; only arm's-length, contractually documented charges are deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to the Taiwan parent must satisfy the arm's-length standard and be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; management fees without real service substance are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 7 - 资产减值损失 Asset Impairment Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impairment of receivables, software intangibles, and other assets; tax adjustments apply where accounting impairment exceeds tax-recognized amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Impairment charges related to intercompany receivables from the Taiwan group must be supported by evidence of collectability assessment; artificial bad debts from related-party balances will be adjusted on audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 15 - 纳税调整增加额 Tax Adjustment Increases
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenditures, entertainment expenses exceeding the 60%/5%o caps, non-arm's-length charges, and expenses not supported by valid invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entertainment and indirect charges allocated by the Taiwan parent must be allocated on a reasonable basis with documentary evidence; failing this, full add-back plus 50%-500% penalty exposure follows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 17 - 免税、减计收入及加计扣除 Exempt Income, Deemed Income and Super Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Software enterprise tax holiday, R&D 100% super deduction, and other incentives claimed on Annex A107012 (R&D super deduction schedule).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The software two-year exemption/three-year half-rate incentive requires a valid software enterprise certificate and substantially domestic software development activity; overstated headcount in payroll automation R&D will trigger clawback.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 19 - 弥补以前年度亏损 Loss Carry-Forward Offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsets against taxable income of losses incurred in the immediately preceding five years, per Article 18 EIT Law; ten-year carry-forward for qualifying High/New-Tech enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the Taiwan parent cannot be offset against the WFOE's China taxable income; only the WFOE's own carried losses may be utilized, with audit verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 20 - 应纳税所得额 Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit adjusted by net tax adjustments and incentives; the base to which the 25% headline rate (or applicable preferential rate) is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE consistently reports zero or minimal taxable income while exporting high-value payroll services to the group, tax authorities will initiate a transfer pricing risk screening; the taxpayer bears the burden of proof.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 23 - 减免所得税额 Tax Reduction Amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reductions arising from the 15% preferential rate, software 两免三减半 benefit, and other incentive schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Documentation (software enterprise certificate, high-tech certificate) must be attached; non-resident ownership does not bar the incentives but entity-level substance must be verifiable by on-site inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Line 27 - 应补（退）所得税额 Balance of Tax Due or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as final tax liability less quarterly prepayments; if in excess, payment is due by the statutory deadline; if refundable, application follows the annual settlement review.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refund claims are subject to tax authority verification; a refund arising at the same time as large outbound dividend remittances to Taiwan may trigger a full anti-avoidance review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to RMB 2,000 for ordinary cases and RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases (Tax Collection Law Art. 62); daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax (approx. 18.25% per annum) (Art. 32); under-declaration or evasion: additional assessment plus a penalty of 50%-500% of the unpaid tax (Arts. 63-64); criminal liability under Criminal Law Art. 201 (逃避缴纳税款罪) where the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and the ratio exceeds 10% of tax due, with imprisonment up to 7 years in aggravated cases; responsible directors and financial officers face individual punishment and travel bans.
